title: What counts as a breaking change
content: A change is breaking when code that works against the previous version stops working, or keeps working while doing something different. A removed or renamed symbol, a parameter that becomes required, a default that flips, a return shape that changes, a raised exception type that changes, and a dropped runtime version are all breaking. A change to internals with an unchanged public surface is not, however large the diff. Semantic-version labels are evidence, never the decision: maintainers ship breaking changes in patch releases and cosmetic ones in majors.

title: The radar reads, it never upgrades
content: This workflow reports what changed in the libraries it watches. It never edits a dependency file, opens a pull request, or upgrades anything, and it never runs a build to find out whether an upgrade would pass. Acting on a release is the engineer's decision and stays that way.
